A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Weight Space Consolidation with the same authors, core method, and benchmarks. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite retitling and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 experiments, TRACE instruction-tuning results, and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds reset-method comparisons and classification results for training from scratch.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations (4)–(6) retain the same moment-based parameter ranking, soft reset toward previous-task weights, and running weight averaging. The additional reset methods are comparators, not changes to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100, and the same eight TRACE tasks. The added comparisons use retained classification data and memory budgets; they introduce no new domain or task requirements.

E2.justification: v4 Table 5 adds Shrink & Perturb and Continual Backpropagation to the reset comparison. Table 6 adds From Scratch to the classification-accuracy comparison, although joint training already appeared in v3's training-loss analysis. The principal vision and TRACE comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 Table 6 introduces an accuracy comparison using fresh initialization versus continual Replay and WSC at matched memory sizes of 20, 100, 200, 300, and 400 exemplars per class. Existing benchmark splits, architectures, and hyperparameter-transfer protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The reset analysis gains comparisons with established plasticity-recovery methods, and Table 6 examines when training from scratch helps or hurts as memory increases. Existing component, importance-metric, reset-frequency, forgetting, and sparsity analyses remain; the sparsity analysis moves to Appendix A.4.

E5.justification: v3 provides only point estimates for TRACE. v4 Table 9 adds per-task uncertainty for replay and merging methods and identifies it as standard error across five runs, substantially expanding statistical reporting to the language experiments. Class-IL captions also identify existing uncertainty values as standard errors. This does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds reset-baseline scores and From Scratch accuracy results. Table 6 reports From Scratch versus WSC at 69.96 versus 74.49 with 200 exemplars, but 78.94 versus 77.71 with 400. Retained class-IL tables match exactly. In TRACE, Avg. (Offline) FOMC accuracy at 20% memory changes from 0.00 in v3 Table 7 to 0.02 in v4 Table 9.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(16), local strong-convexity assumption, stability/plasticity derivations, and parameter-importance formulas are retained. The expanded discussion of training from scratch introduces no new proof or formal result.

C1.justification: v4 more explicitly centers the contribution on abundant but incomplete memory and claims a scalable alternative to full retraining. It adds memory-spectrum analysis to the contribution list. The central reset-and-averaging proposal, vision/language applicability, and computational-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 interprets Table 6 as showing that training from scratch inadequately preserves past knowledge with incomplete memory, whereas retaining previous models helps. This qualifies the benefits of full-memory resetting. The privacy, streaming, and task-boundary limitations are unchanged and move from Section 6 to Appendix A.7.

D1.justification: Figure 2(b) and Section 3.2 newly specify full exemplar memory for the existing training-loss experiment, previously described as sufficient memory. This clarifies documentation rather than establishing a changed experiment. Appendix A.5 retains the hyperparameters, software, model sizes, and hardware; asset disclosures are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a dedicated positioning discussion and Table 1 comparing prior work across memory regimes, computational constraints, plasticity, and forgetting. Reset-related positioning is substantially expanded. References add Ash and Adams, Galashov et al., and Cho et al., while removing Tang et al.'s sequential model-merging paper.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, with substantial rewrites of the abstract, introductory framing, and conclusion. It adds a positioning subsection, reorganizes the ablation narrative, moves TRACE descriptions, sparsity discussion, and limitations into the appendix, and switches to author-year citations.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document template and extensively rearranges displays. It adds positioning and From Scratch tables, expands the reset table, and relocates the TRACE bar chart and sparsity plot. v3 Figure 11 incorrectly duplicates the CIFAR plot under an ImageNet caption; v4 Figure 9 replaces it with the ImageNet accuracy/time display.

improvement.justification: The added reset-method and From Scratch comparisons strengthen the justification for WSC, and correcting the ImageNet plot removes a misleading duplicate. These provide limited gains while the core method and benchmark findings remain stable. The new TRACE uncertainty reporting needs clarification: Replay's FOMC entry of 0.01 ± 0.05 is incompatible with the usual mean-and-standard-error interpretation for nonnegative accuracy scores, limiting its value as improved statistical evidence.
